question: What does the CLSU student-thesis abstract report about goby identifications and Central Luzon scope, and what is still missing for province- or waterbody-level fish records?

source.titleAsIndexed: Species Differentiation of Philippine Goby Through Morphology and Polymerase Chain Reaction-Restricted Fragment Length Polymorphism
source.institutionalRecord: Central Luzon State University College of Veterinary Science and Medicine, Research and Publications / Student Thesis section
source.recordAccessNote: The current research page is dynamically rendered. Its rendered text did not expose this thesis entry during direct open; the title, year, adviser metadata and abstract were available in the official page's indexed result returned for the thesis title and goby terms. Treat this as an institutional abstract record, not review of the thesis manuscript.
source.itemSpecificLicense: No thesis text license or reuse permission was identified. Publicly indexed metadata is not permission to republish the abstract, thesis, images, sequences, or results.

scope.studyAreaAsIndexed: Different inland waters in Central Luzon
scope.reportedMethod: The abstract describes morphological meristic examination and PCR-RFLP analysis of the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I gene. The thesis methods and sample records were not reviewed.

sourceReportedTaxa.identityStatus: The abstract gives two alternative names for the goby identification; it does not resolve the identity or pair an individual name with an individual province or waterbody.
The indexed record contains spacing/spelling noise, including another variant in its abstract text. The proposed search spelling is not a taxonomic correction or independent specimen identification.
Author-reported abstract identification only; no voucher, sequence accession, site, or independent specimen review was located.

findings: The institutional index describes a 2012 student thesis using morphology and PCR-RFLP on gobies from inland waters in Central Luzon.
Its indexed abstract names all seven Region III provinces in its broad scope, but supplies no locality-to-specimen crosswalk or waterbody names.
The first goby label is explicitly unresolved between two alternatives, and the other labels remain author-reported without specimen or accession linkage.

The thesis year is not a verified sampling year. The study's counts, collection dates, effort, sequence accessions, diagnostic images, site allocations and item-specific reuse terms are unavailable in the indexed record.
evidenceLimits: Province-level wording does not establish that each named taxon was collected in each province; the abstract assigns the five-province list to an unresolved alternative label and does not show individual sample rows.
The record cannot establish presence in a named river, stream, lake, reservoir, or other waterbody, current presence, native status, or distribution boundaries.
Do not treat the two alternative goby names as synonyms or as two verified species based on this abstract.
No taxonomic identity, occurrence, abundance, diet, catchability, geometry, image, safety, legal, or public-app assertion is admitted.
nextAction: Keep the institutional abstract as a seven-province discovery lead. If a full thesis or supplementary accession list becomes lawfully available, inspect the original sample-to-province and sample-to-waterbody crosswalk, vouchers/accessions, collection dates, and diagnostic evidence before creating any taxon-level record. Continue freshwater inventory work through independently site-resolved sources; Central Luzon and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: Official Central Luzon State University College of Veterinary Science and Medicine Research and Publications page; the search-indexed student-thesis record supplies the title, author/year/adviser metadata, abstract methods, source-reported labels, and broad provincial scope. The current direct page text extraction does not expose the dynamic record.
